questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience both the urban, and cultural life in the city but I also wanted to have the opportunity to have to experience an outdoor lifestyle by having easy access to nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of emails about the first days - both about social events and practical stuff from the University

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assigned a supervisor from the international student office who I was invited to contact if I had any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just filled out an application and listed the different accommodations and got one of my most prioritized

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
it's nice to feel that your entire stay is not just about being a student. Being off campus means that you in another way segregate your student life and your private life. 
You also get to know more of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was an online form you just had to fill out. There was also an accompanying document that elaborated on some of the various requirements.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It difficult for me to remember all detail about the process. In the online form, you had to provide information about passed exams, approval of subjects from your home university. You also had to write a motivated application, etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier we had a supervisor from the international student office who we could email and book a meeting with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of problems getting relevant courses as I was not on a subject-specific study abroad. I couldn't get enrolled in any of the landscape architecture courses as I was told that these were full. I ended up getting an email to one of the teachers at the relevant courses and we organized an unofficial meeting. She ended up pulling some strings so that I could get enrolled in the relevant courses. Overall it was a quite frustrating process as I chose to go to Edinburgh because one can study Landscape architecture.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If one struggles to get the write courses before getting to the country it is easier to wait till you get there. Usually every thing falls into place.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were too easy but I also took courses on first year

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is quite the same: a combination of coursework, fieldwork, studio work, tutorials, pinups, and critics.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Landscape Architecture Theory 1B
Landscape Architecture Design 1B
Landscape Architecture Technique 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Landscape Architecture Design 1B
It is a very interesting course where you work on a site outside Edinburgh. It is very interesting to design for an environment different from Denmark

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of cultural, athletic and social societies you cold join

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: West-African dance, and the hillwalking society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to a Ceilidh event - its the best

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Skotland is not very different from Denmark. In many ways, we share humor, values, political approaches, and so on.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I went to a ceilidh event and met a group of Scottish people they invited into a group chat of locals and they all became my friends. 
Remember that it's not only the exchange student events you should go to. Try to do something outside what the university is offering.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only the Scottish accent - especially when they use slang

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Overall Scottish people are very friendly and chatty. You also just feel very safe in Scotland

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It's ok to approach people and invite people out on a "friend date"
You don't have to go to all events in the beginning to make friends... 
Everything (paperwork, course-enrollment..) most often falls into place when you get to the country

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Becoming friends with so many locals. I really got to understand the culture and the language much better.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, some days just feel weird when it's cold and dark and you don't want to go to another exchange student speed dating event.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
